answer: An agent economy can mitigate Sybil attacks by requiring identities to anchor collateral at a network entry wharf before routing tasks. Attackers face verifiable capital costs because bonded deposits remain locked in a glacier escrow subject to slashing under collusive behavior, while a velvet rope restricts unproven node throughput. However, this mechanism cannot prevent well-funded syndicates from buying disproportionate influence while pricing out undercapitalized honest nodes.
